deciding_marker_or_seam: The repeated anger question opens the exchange; Jonah's answer is met by the vine-to-city pity comparison, which closes the book as an unanswered interrogative.
boundary_rationale: Question, reply, countercomparison, and final open question are inseparable dialogue turns; preserving the unanswered close prevents an imposed ethical or theological answer.
rejected_alternative: Separating 4:9 from 4:10-11 would detach prompt and reply from their interpretation; isolating 4:11 would strip the final question of the vine comparison.
defensible_basis: Repeated dialogue formula, direct reply, second-person/first-person comparison, and deliberately unanswered interrogative produce a strong closing unit.

source_observations.text: God said to Jonah, “Is it right for you to be angry about the vine?” He said, “I am right to be angry, even to death.”

Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred twenty thousand persons who can’t discern between their right hand and their left hand, and also many animals?”
